title: An ambient catalytic solid that fixes nitrogen at industrial intensity

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a durable catalytic solid, or a stable reactive interface on a solid, that converts nitrogen gas into ammonia at ambient temperature and atmospheric pressure with industrial productivity and overall energy consumption competitive with Haber–Bosch. It must selectively make ammonia despite competing hydrogen production, and the nitrogen in the product must demonstrably come from the supplied N2. The target is the simultaneous achievement of these properties in a working system; ambient operation or high selectivity alone would not establish it.

The scope includes catalytic interphases such as those used in lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction, rather than requiring an isolated solid to perform every chemical step unaided. Nevertheless, the surrounding electrochemical process must satisfy the productivity, durability and energy requirements. Producing ammonia from nitrate, releasing nitrogen already present in a catalyst, or modestly improving a conventional high-pressure catalyst would not demonstrate the specified conversion of N2 under ambient conditions.

significance.text: Haber–Bosch supplies ammonia for fertilizer through predominantly centralized plants using high-temperature, high-pressure synthesis. Achieving the proposed capability would provide a fundamentally different synthesis route that removes the need for that reactor while retaining industrial productivity and competitive energy consumption. The revolutionary feature would be this combination of operating conditions and performance, rather than a small improvement in catalyst activity.

Such a route could enable modular ammonia production closer to fertilizer users and could supply ammonia for fuel or energy-carrier applications. These are conditional deployment possibilities, not automatic consequences of discovering a catalyst. Economical distributed production would still depend on electricity and feedstock costs, product concentration and separation, equipment reliability, and local demand. Fuel applications would additionally depend on downstream storage, distribution and conversion infrastructure.

Synthesis: the meaningful comparison with Haber–Bosch is a complete ammonia-production system operating on comparable accounting boundaries. A reactor that works at room temperature can still consume excessive electricity or require costly purification and separation. Likewise, a selective laboratory electrode operating at low output would not by itself establish an industrial alternative. The innovation would change the available production architecture; its eventual economic and environmental impact would remain dependent on the system built around it.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central capability to establish is selective, sustained nitrogen activation at ambient temperature and pressure at a useful production rate. In aqueous electrochemical systems, nitrogen reduction competes with hydrogen chemistry, including competition for adsorption at the surface. A successful material and interface must favor ammonia formation while continuing to supply reactants and remove products fast enough for device-scale productivity. High selectivity and high ammonia output are separate requirements.

Proving nitrogen provenance is an equally concrete barrier. NOx impurities and nitrogen-containing electrodes, catalysts, electrolytes, solvents or preparation residues can generate apparent ammonia production without genuine reduction of the supplied N2. These are documented false-positive mechanisms; they do not, by themselves, establish deliberate fabrication. Reliable demonstrations require quantitative contamination measurements and isotope experiments showing that ammonia derived from 15N2 agrees with ordinary-N2 experiments in rate and selectivity under matched conditions.

Lithium-mediated routes provide a better-verified starting point, but their energy losses are substantial. The 2024 review attributes an intrinsic efficiency limit of approximately 28% to the roughly 3 V driving force required for lithium reduction. A highly selective interphase therefore does not automatically solve the energy problem: Faradaic efficiency describes how charge is allocated to the desired product, whereas energy efficiency also reflects the energy expended to drive the process. Meeting the proposed Haber–Bosch comparison would require overcoming the limitations described for established lithium-mediated operation or developing a different route.

Synthesis: the remaining engineering challenge is integration. Industrial productivity, stable interfaces, verified nitrogen provenance and competitive overall energy consumption must be demonstrated together under ambient conditions. Multi-day operation is already reported for some lithium-mediated systems, so duration alone cannot define the breakthrough. The supplied evidence identifies these barriers but does not establish whether the full combination remains absent across the entire field in November 2026.

current_state.text: Choi et al., Nature Communications 11, 5546, published on 3 November 2020, assessed 127 aqueous nitrogen-reduction papers published through April 2020. They reported that none met all three of their criteria for ammonia yield, quantitative isotope verification and NOx control. They left the feasibility of direct aqueous N2 reduction open and regarded lithium-mediated routes in organic electrolytes as better verified. This was a dated assessment of the surveyed literature, not proof that aqueous reduction is impossible or that every reported signal was false. The conclusion is explicitly stated in the main article and does not require reconstructing the supplementary color coding.

Chang, Jain, Rezaie and Manthiram’s review, published on 11 March 2024 in Nature Catalysis 7, 231–241, describes lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction as producing ammonia under ambient conditions. The supplied review identifies the journal-site material as a subscription preview containing the abstract and references, while the NSF-hosted copy contains all eleven journal-formatted pages. That complete copy reports selectivities up to 99% at 15 bar and energy efficiencies up to 14%. These are review-level reports of separate performance metrics, not evidence that one device achieved both maxima simultaneously. In particular, 15 bar is elevated pressure and cannot substantiate the ambient-pressure requirement.

Chu, Yang and Shin’s 2025 ChemSusChem review compares a maximum theoretical lithium-mediated energy efficiency of about 28% with approximately 56–62% for modern Haber–Bosch plants. The supplied review locates this comparison in the Introduction of retained full-text XML, correcting the earlier description of abstract-only access. The article also summarizes multi-day operation, including 300 hours under potential cycling. That endurance result demonstrates durability progress under its reported operating protocol; it does not establish simultaneous ambient-pressure industrial productivity and Haber–Bosch energy parity.

The 2025 review gives a 13% energy-efficiency summary for a continuous-flow study, whereas the 2024 review reports efficiencies up to 14%. The supplied materials do not explain that difference, so the figures should remain attributed to their respective reviews rather than being reconciled by assumption. The underlying experiments were not independently assessed in the supplied evidence review. More broadly, these sources establish dated achievements and limitations, but the supplied freshness-search record is empty: they cannot establish a comprehensive field-wide conclusion as of 1 November 2026. This coverage limitation does not invalidate the reported results.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification framework: an earth-abundant catalytic solid or interphase should produce ammonia from supplied N2 at ambient temperature and atmospheric pressure, with contamination controls grounded in Choi et al. These should include measurement of NOx alongside ammonia, accounting for nitrogen-containing experimental components, and quantitative 15N2 experiments over several durations. The labeled-ammonia production rate and selectivity should agree with corresponding ordinary-N2 experiments under identical conditions. Earth abundance is a proposed practical requirement, rather than part of that paper’s complete benchmark package.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed verification framework

completion_criteria.text: A proposed early laboratory milestone is at least 10 nmol s−1 cm−2 of geometric electrode area, the favorable threshold used by Choi et al. This must be distinguished from completion at industrial intensity. Their paper cites device targets of approximately 100–930 nmol s−1 cm−2, also normalized to geometric electrode area, and explicitly places its laboratory threshold at least an order of magnitude below industrially relevant targets. A convincing industrial demonstration should select and justify a device productivity target for its intended application rather than treating 10 nmol s−1 cm−2 as sufficient or the cited range as a universal standard.
completion_criteria.label: A proposed early laboratory milestone is at least

completion_criteria.text: Proposal: the same operating system should demonstrate overall energy consumption no greater than a specified Haber–Bosch comparator, using matched boundaries for feed preparation, energy inputs, product recovery and product specification. It should report ammonia output, Faradaic efficiency where applicable, energy consumption and degradation throughout a predefined multi-day run. Ambient temperature and pressure, the duration, and acceptable performance drift should be fixed before testing. These are proposed acceptance conditions, not an established field standard, and a multi-day result alone would not establish commercial service life.
completion_criteria.label: Proposal

completion_criteria.text: Proposal: independent laboratories should reproduce the central result using sufficiently documented materials, apparatus, contamination measurements and operating procedures. Tests should establish the range of feed purity, operating conditions and scale over which the claimed performance holds, including whether performance survives product collection and separation. Such finite demonstrations would establish reproducibility and demonstrated operating breadth, not literal universality across materials, devices or environments.
completion_criteria.label: Proposal

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: MAS-04, “A reliable map from a property specification to a makeable material,” could help identify catalysts and interphases satisfying the competing requirements of nitrogen activation, selectivity and stability. MAS-03, “General atomically precise covalent construction,” could offer control over catalytic sites or their surroundings. Both concern broader capabilities for discovering or constructing materials; MAS-08 concerns a particular chemical conversion and requires a verified production process even if its catalyst can be designed precisely.

Roster-based synthesis: MAS-06, “Reversible solids that store energy at chemical-fuel specific energy,” shares an energy-system connection because ammonia can serve as an energy carrier. The distinction is functional: MAS-06 concerns reversible energy storage in solids, whereas MAS-08 concerns synthesizing ammonia from nitrogen gas. Successful ammonia synthesis would not establish the storage material, reversibility or specific-energy capability required by MAS-06.

Roster-based synthesis: MAS-02, “Bulk structural solids that are both near their ideal strength and damage-tolerant,” MAS-05, “Structural solids that remain engineering materials after fusion-level atomic displacement,” and MAS-09, “Structural metals that fully recover from macroscopic fracture in service,” all involve maintaining useful material performance under demanding conditions. Their mechanical strength, radiation-damage and fracture-recovery targets remain distinct from the chemical stability and selectivity of a nitrogen-fixing interface. MAS-07, “Programmable growth of load-bearing solids,” concerns controlled structural growth; catalyst fabrication could benefit from improved manufacturing control, but nitrogen fixation does not demonstrate programmable structural growth.

Roster-based synthesis: MAS-01, “Ambient-pressure room-temperature superconductivity in a manufacturable solid,” and MAS-10, “Topologically protected quantum matter outside the dilution refrigerator,” share the ambition of obtaining valuable material behavior under more accessible operating conditions. Their defining advances concern electronic or quantum properties, whereas MAS-08 concerns catalytic chemistry and process performance. Ambient operation is a shared deployment aspiration, not evidence of a common mechanism or completion criterion.

change_log.change: Preserved MAS-08 and its title while defining the target as a catalytic solid or stable interphase within a complete ammonia-production system.
change_log.reason: The review supports including lithium-mediated interphases and identifies simultaneous productivity, selectivity, provenance, durability and energy performance as the distinctive scope.

change_log.change: Corrected the 2020 paper’s attribution from Du et al. to Choi et al. and specified its literature cutoff of April 2020.
change_log.reason: The supplied review verifies Choi as first author and bounds the assessment to 127 papers available through that date.

change_log.change: Replaced language suggesting experiments were easy to fake with an explanation of documented contamination-driven false positives.
change_log.reason: The evidence establishes alternative nitrogen sources and analytical pitfalls, not deliberate fabrication.

change_log.change: Separated Faradaic selectivity, ammonia productivity and energy efficiency, and distinguished ambient operation from the 15-bar selectivity result.
change_log.reason: High selectivity does not establish low energy consumption, industrial output or atmospheric-pressure performance.

change_log.change: Corrected source-access descriptions for the 2024 and 2025 reviews and attributed numerical results to the retained review texts.
change_log.reason: The supplied review identifies a partial journal preview, a complete journal-formatted NSF copy, and full-text ChemSusChem XML; the efficiency comparison appears in the latter’s Introduction.

change_log.change: Added the reported 300-hour potential-cycling result and retained the unexplained 13% versus 14% efficiency difference.
change_log.reason: The endurance result is meaningful progress, while the supplied evidence does not justify reconciling the efficiency summaries or combining separate achievements.

change_log.change: Replaced the categorical present-day absence claim with a dated, bounded assessment.
change_log.reason: The empty freshness-search record cannot establish complete field status as of November 2026.

change_log.change: Separated the 10 nmol s−1 cm−2 laboratory milestone from the approximately 100–930 nmol s−1 cm−2 device targets and retained geometric-area normalization.
change_log.reason: The lower threshold does not demonstrate the industrial intensity required by the concept.

change_log.change: Made distributed fertilizer production and ammonia fuel deployment conditional, and expanded the proposed demonstration framework.
change_log.reason: Deployment depends on systems economics and infrastructure; convincing completion also requires matched energy accounting, predefined durability conditions and independent reproduction.

change_log.change: Added explicit distinctions with all other supplied roster entries, labeling those relationships as synthesis.
change_log.reason: The roster supplies concept identities but no evidence establishing dependencies or shared mechanisms.

unresolved_issues: Whether any development after the supplied 2024–2025 reviews achieves the full combination of ambient conditions, industrial productivity, verified nitrogen provenance, durability and competitive overall energy consumption remains unresolved; no freshness-search coverage was supplied.
The supplied reviews do not explain the difference between the 2024 report of energy efficiencies up to 14% and the 2025 summary of 13% for a continuous-flow study.

The underlying experiments supporting the review-level performance and endurance summaries were not independently assessed in the supplied evidence review; simultaneous achievement of their separate metrics is not established.

The proposed completion framework still requires an application-specific productivity target, a precise ambient operating window, a predefined durability duration and degradation limit, an earth-abundance definition, and a Haber–Bosch comparator with matched energy-accounting boundaries.
